input: page-sheet.json only. Chosen before any prose is written.

sections.why: States the page's one claim: your network has an inside, an outside, and one door. Short, sets up the picture.

rejected.why: A numbers strip performs precision before the reader has the model.

sections.why: The reader runs real commands on their own machine. Code is the only honest form for commands.

rejected.why: A paraphrased command is not runnable; the honest form is the command itself.

sections.why: Three reserved ranges with what they look like at home. Lookup-shaped content.

rejected.why: Three ranges compare as rows; prose turns them into memorization.

sections.why: The visual need is spatial: devices inside a subnet, a router with two sides, the internet outside. The diagram block is a linear list and cannot show two sides of a boundary, so an authored figure is used.

rejected.why: Devices in a subnet and a router with two sides are a layout, not a sequence.

sections.why: The apartment analogy explains subnet and router jobs in one connected story.

rejected.why: The apartment analogy carries the model; a callout marks it optional.

sections.why: Three jobs, each with what it does and where you see it. Parallel rows.

rejected.why: The three jobs are parallel duties, not an ordered procedure.

sections.why: One request out and back is a strict sequence. This is exactly what the linear diagram is for.

rejected.why: One request out and back is strictly linear; a static figure adds nothing.

sections.why: One right answer: which address is local.

rejected.why: Which-address-is-local has one right answer; an open blank cannot check it.

sections.why: The reader writes down their own values, which the rest of the series reuses.

rejected.why: The reader's own addresses have no key; scoring them is meaningless.

sections.why: Private ranges and NAT behavior come from standards; link them.

rejected.why: A standards quote without the link list cannot be followed up.

sections.why: Points to listeners on one machine.

rejected.why: The page owes a pointer to the listeners lesson, not a silent rule line.
